text:
sara: Quick follow-up from the autoscaler sync — we need to decide where the request priority ledger lives and who owns mutation/read semantics. I sketched two options: 1) central ledger owned by orch operator, scaler reads (RPC). 2) ledger as a thin delegated store per-pool, orchestrator syncs for global view. Thoughts?

mike: Option 2 seems nicer for isolating tenants, less cross-pool contention. but how do we keep global fairness?

akshay: If we use per-pool ledgers we need a reconciliation step that is eventual but accounts for headroom. otherwise bursts can double-spend credits.

ellie: can we push the fairness logic into the admission API instead of the ledger? i.e., ledger stores raw tokens, admission applies global rules fetched periodically. cheaper reads.

sara: yeah that maps to two design axes: ownership (orch vs pool) and policy enforcement (admission vs ledger). I worry about latency if admission needs cross-pool lookups on every request.

mike: agree. perf constraints: admission must respond <50ms p95. cross-pool RPCs will kill that. so keep hot path local.

akshay: variant: local ledger for hot path, compact deltas streamed to central aggregator for accounting and fairness adjustments. aggregator only triggers corrections, not on-path checks.

ellie: that sounds promising. aggregator can emit corrective tokens or throttle signals. also useful for billing.

sara: prototype sketch (very small):
```proto
message LedgerDelta {
  string pool_id = 1;
  string tenant_id = 2;
  int64 tokens_used = 3;
  int64 epoch = 4; // monotonic
}
service LedgerStream {
  rpc StreamDeltas(stream LedgerDelta) returns (stream Ack);
}
```
local ledger increments on admission; stream sends batches. central aggregator reconciles epochs.

mike: question: who applies preemption or throttling when aggregator detects imbalance? orch operator should, but we need an immediate fast-fail too.

akshay: local admission can apply soft-shields (tenant-level queueing) based on local ledger. aggregator issues hard-corrections (reduce future bucket).

ellie: we should also surface a 'debt' metric so product teams can see when we applied corrections. put it in console + metrics.

deploy-bot: deploy started: ledger-streamer v0.1 -> canary (sha: abcd123) :rocket:

mike: small nit: epochs need to be signed to prevent reorder weirdness. attach last-ack nonce from aggregator in responses.

akshay: agreed. also keep delta idempotent keys for replay protection.

sara: tradeoffs recap: local-ledger = low-latency admission, eventual global fairness; central-ledger = simpler global correctness but higher latency and single point of contention. hybrid (local + aggregator) gives best perf with complexity in reconciliation.

ellie: implementation tasks? i can draft ledger-stream proto + metrics dashboard. mike can prototype local admission fast-path. akshay help with aggregator alg (leaky-bucket reconciliation).

mike: acked. will drop a short perf microbench (local RPC vs none) by tomorrow.

akshay: i'll write reconciliation pseudo-code and failure modes doc (replays, network partitions).

sara: great. action items + owners: ellie proto + metrics, mike perf bench, akshay reconciliation doc. I'll follow up with a short RFC update and sequencing plan. :thumbsup:

ellie: +1

mike: +1

akshay: +1

sara: leaving this thread open for any blockers, otherwise i'll fold notes into the RFC later today.
